title: Jyotirmayee Nayak Wins Indian Idol 16, Becomes First Contestant From Odisha to Lift the Trophy
excerpt: The 24-year-old singer, who used music therapy to help cancer patients before auditioning, took home Rs 20 lakh and dedicated her victory to the people she healed through song.
body:
• Jyotirmayee Nayak, 24, from Odisha has been crowned the winner of Indian Idol Season 16, taking home the trophy and Rs 20 lakh
  • Tanishk Shukla from Jabalpur finished as first runner-up in the two-day grand finale aired on July 25–26
  • Nayak is the first contestant from Odisha to win the show and credited her victory to the cancer patients she healed through music therapy
  • The season, themed 'Yaadon Ki Playlist' and judged by Shreya Ghoshal, Vishal Dadlani and Badshah, ran for 10 months and earned two extensions

An Emotional Finale Caps a Historic Season

https://youtube.com/watch?v=yMA1ZCcoUMQ

After ten months of performances, eliminations and emotional moments that earned the show two broadcast extensions, Indian Idol Season 16 crowned its winner on Saturday night. Jyotirmayee Nayak, a 24-year-old singer from Odisha, took the trophy and Rs 20 lakh in prize money with a breathtaking rendition of "Saiyaan O Saiyaan" in the grand finale on Sony Entertainment Television.

Tanishk Shukla from Jabalpur emerged as the first runner-up. The two-day finale, aired on July 25 and 26, featured performances from all six finalists — Nayak, Shukla, Anshika Chonkar, Manraj Veer Singh, Myscmme Bosu and Suhail — before the judges declared the winner.

"Winning Indian Idol Season 16 feels absolutely surreal. From walking into the auditions with nothing but a dream to standing here as the winner, this journey has truly been life-changing."

— Jyotirmayee Nayak, Indian Idol 16 winner

From Music Therapy to the Biggest Stage

Nayak's journey to the Indian Idol stage began far from television cameras. Before auditioning, she dedicated herself to working with cancer patients, using music therapy to bring comfort and hope to people undergoing treatment. Upon winning, she credited her victory not to her training or talent alone, but to the patients who inspired her.

https://x.com/achyuta_samanta/status/2081416536397623782

"This trophy is not just mine; it belongs to everyone who stood by me and made this dream possible," she said. "I hope to continue making music that touches hearts, keeps me learning, and makes everyone proud."

Away from the reality show circuit, Nayak is already an established name in the Odia music industry. Her journey on Indian Idol was marked by memorable performances — her rendition of "O Jab Tak Hai Jaan Jaane Jahan Main Nachungi" earned a standing ovation from veteran actress Hema Malini, while "Jaane Kyun Log Mohabbat Kiya Karte Hain" became a fan favourite.

A Season That Refused to End

Season 16, themed 'Yaadon Ki Playlist,' struck a chord with viewers that few recent reality shows have matched. Judged by Shreya Ghoshal, Vishal Dadlani and Badshah, the season ran for over nine months and was extended twice due to sustained audience demand — a rarity in Indian television, where shows routinely struggle to maintain ratings past a few months.

The finale itself was a star-studded affair, with guest appearances and tributes alongside the competitive performances. The season drew particular attention for its emotional storytelling, with contestants' personal narratives often resonating as powerfully as their vocal performances.

Breaking New Ground for Odisha

Nayak's victory holds special significance for Odisha's music community. She is the first contestant from the state to win Indian Idol in the show's 16-season history, a milestone that has drawn congratulations from fans and musicians across the Odia-speaking world.

The win comes at a time when regional music industries across India are gaining wider recognition, with streaming platforms and social media helping artists from smaller states reach national audiences. For Nayak, the path forward includes her ambition of playback singing in Bollywood — she has publicly expressed a desire to sing for actress Alia Bhatt.

Looking back, she said the journey was not without its difficult moments. Landing among the bottom contestants during elimination rounds hit her hard emotionally, but the outpouring of support from viewers kept her going week after week. Her parents, she said, never stopped believing in her dream.
